title: Beef and cabbage keema with potatoes

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a plain whole food or cupboard staple, and curry powder, tinned tomatoes and frozen peas are all things a grandparent would keep.

supermarket.reason: Beef mince, white cabbage, potatoes, peas, yoghurt and curry powder are everyday Tesco items at ordinary prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only one casserole, a knife and a board, with simple softening, browning and simmering.

works.reason: 500g mince, 500g potatoes, half a cabbage and peas make a generous four portions, and a tin of tomatoes plus 300ml water suits a 20-minute covered simmer before the cabbage goes in.

honest_times.reason: 25 minutes covers slicing onions, cubing potatoes, shredding cabbage and the softening and browning, and 20 plus 10 minutes of simmering matches the 30 cook minutes.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the lemon from the March fresh list, is used in the steps, and nothing unlisted appears apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warming one-pot curry suits early March, and half a white cabbage is a main component named in the title rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a filling family meal of beef, potatoes, cabbage and peas with a yoghurt topping, with plenty of vegetables and protein.
